pr.title: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain

raw_findings.body: `website_name` is declared as a plain attribute gated only by `include_website_name` (`website.present?`), so the user's website host/path is serialized and exposed to anonymous viewers even though the raw `website` attribute is deliberately hidden for restricted TL0 users, defeating the anti-spam restriction.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Privacy/anti-spam restriction on user website is bypassed for anonymous viewers.
raw_findings.impact: `website_name` is declared as a plain attribute gated only by `include_website_name` (`website.present?`), so the user's website host/path is serialized and exposed to anonymous viewers even though the raw `website` attribute is deliberately hidden for restricted TL0 users, defeating the anti-spam restriction.
raw_findings.root_cause: New attribute `website_name` derives from the restricted `website` field but was registered as a normal attribute instead of an untrusted one.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` declaration (or make `include_website_name` also return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), so it is withheld under the same conditions as `website`.
raw_findings.title: website_name leaks restricted website to anonymous viewers of TL0 users
raw_findings.trigger: An anonymous request serializes a TL0 user whose `website` profile field is set; `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true so `website` itself is withheld via `untrusted_attributes`.

raw_findings.body: The equal-length subdomain comparison logic (`website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`) is unverified, so a regression that returns the wrong host or full path would pass CI undetected.
raw_findings.evidence: it "returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain" do
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested conditional branch allows silent regressions.
raw_findings.impact: The equal-length subdomain comparison logic (`website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`) is unverified, so a regression that returns the wrong host or full path would pass CI undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: Added tests cover only the equal-host, else, and non-matching cases but omit the equal-label subdomain branch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a spec case stubbing `Discourse.current_hostname` to e.g. `forum.example.com` with a website like `http://www.example.com/user` asserting the expected `website_name`, plus a negative case where base domains differ.
raw_findings.title: No test covers same-base-domain subdomain branch of website_name
raw_findings.trigger: The `elsif` branch in `website_name` (both hosts have equal, >2 label counts, e.g. website `www.example.com` vs instance `forum.example.com`) is exercised only in production, never in the spec.

finding.title: website_name leaks restricted website to anonymous viewers of TL0 users
finding.trigger: An anonymous request serializes a TL0 user whose `website` profile field is set; `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true so `website` itself is withheld via `untrusted_attributes`.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds `:website_name` at line 43 as a regular attribute. The repository context shows `untrusted_attributes` (lines 25-33) defines `include_X?` methods that return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The existing spec at line 11 lists `website` among untrusted_attributes but `website_name` is not added there. The `include_website_name` method (line 153 per evidence) only checks `website.present?`, not `restrict_user_fields?`. This allows `website_name` to be serialized for TL0 users viewed anonymously while `website` itself is withheld.
